title: Find the Maximum Length of Valid Subsequence II
summary: Given an integer array nums and a positive integer k, find the maximum length of a subsequence where the sum of every two consecutive elements modulo k is constant.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a positive integer k, find the maximum length of a subsequence where the sum of every two consecutive elements modulo k is constant. Return this length.
constraints: nums is nonempty and k is positive.
Choose a subsequence in input order such that every adjacent chosen pair has the same sum remainder modulo k.
Return the maximum possible subsequence length.
hints: Fix the common pair-sum remainder t; if the new value has remainder r, its predecessor must have remainder t-r.
Maintain the best length by ending remainder and chosen target remainder.
For each r and t, dp[r][t]=max(dp[r][t],dp[(t-r)%k][t]+1).
The recurrence appends the current index to every and only compatible prior state; taking all targets covers every valid subsequence.

tests.explanation: Every adjacent sum in the full sequence is odd, so all five values are valid.
Dynamic programming selects the longest chain having one fixed adjacent-sum remainder.
